pro_course_detail.description:

pro_course_detail.title: How to Succeed in International Business Negotiation
pro_course_detail.description:
Negotiating is a fundamental part of doing business. Making sure you get the best terms for your product or service is essential to making sure your business not just survives, but thrives.
It’s hard enough to negotiate in your own language, but then to have to negotiate in a foreign language such as English?! 

In this lesson we look at your negotiation style and techniques and how you can adopt customs and idioms that are particular to your international environment.  

Objectives: 
- To use common vocabulary used during negotiations
- To introduce common business negotiation idioms (e.g. get down to business, meet half-way)
- To practice being polite (including modal verbs for politeness, the past tense to be polite and other common ways to be polite)
- To practice the use of conditional phrases in negotiations (e.g. as long as, on condition that)
- Vocabulary covered: a show of hands, a win-win situation, meet half-way, stick ot the point, get down to business, have (something) to add, close the deal, diplomatic, final offer, in favor of (something), concern, consideration, under one condition, proposal, consult, decline, interrupt, reconvene, recap, clarify, compromise, mutual, tactful, binding, non-negotiable, unanimous, face-to-face, provision, consensus, tactic, interest, contingency.

pro_course_detail.title: How to Conduct International Business Meetings
pro_course_detail.description:
Business meetings are conducted differently in different parts of the world. Whether you start business right away, engage in small talk, use humor - even something like organizing and how the meetings are followed up are different depending on your country of business. 

In this lesson we look at international business meeting vocabulary, but we also look at how your style of conducting business meetings might vary, depending on where you are and with whom you are meeting. 

Objectives: 
- To use common vocabulary used during different stages of a business meeting (introductions, reviewing past business/meeting notes, discussing items, finishing the meeting)
- To introduce common phrasal verbs used in business meetings (e.g. run out of, reach out)
- To introduce common expressions used in meetings
- To look at different styles of meetings, depending on your country
- Vocabulary covered: small talk, attending, absentees, standing in, tasks, the Chair/chairperson, minutes, prior commitment, run through, take over, go over, move on, agenda, item, input, on the same page, reach out to, break up, brainstorm, run out of (time), close, deal with, come back to (something), punctual, clarification, consensus, objectives, preside over.

This course can be taken at any time, but it is most advantageous to do so before memorizing thousands of words with inaccurate pronunciation, and before spending countless hours practicing bad prosody in conversations.

Depending on your personal goals and what we uncover during our first conversation, we may perfect your consonants, vowels, stress, intonation, rhythm, etc. We can improve all of these at either a basic or advanced level, as needed.

pro_course_detail.title: Step 1: Accent Assessment
pro_course_detail.description:
It is important to note that the Accent Reduction Assessment is a valuable tool used to measure an individual's pronunciation and intonation relative to the Standard American Accent. Upon completion of the assessment, the client will receive a report outlining any existing problems and the severity of each issue for the 44 English-American sounds/phonemes and evaluation of their intonation. The final score will indicate the percentage of correctly pronounced American English sounds/phonemes, with a perfect score being 100, representing the Standard American Accent. It is important to strive for a score as close to 100 as possible, as this indicates a higher level of accuracy in pronunciation and intonation.

The assessment consists of a comprehensive range of English sounds (phonemes). The candidate will read the assessment and provide a speech sample that will be recorded. Afterward, the candidate's performance will be scored, and the results will be shared with the client within five business days.
